content_md:
Simon Willison, in a [note on 18th September 2026](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Sep/18/probably-gonna-eat-you/), returns to his long-running theme that agentic coding tools are only as safe as the blast radius you give them. The framing is characteristically blunt:

> The thing people keep getting wrong is treating the agent like a colleague who might make a mistake. It's not that. It's a very fast, very confident intern who reads everything you point it at — including the parts an attacker wrote — and then acts on all of it with your credentials. If you hand it the keys and walk away, it's probably gonna eat you.

His prescription is unglamorous and familiar: assume anything the model reads is potentially hostile, keep the set of tools it can reach narrow enough to reason about, and don't confuse a sandbox you've configured with a sandbox you've actually tested.
